translations.text: Faith with deeds, desire with constancy, calm with devotion, chastity with humility, fasting with moderation [?],
poverty with generosity, silence with conversation, sharing with equality, endurance without grievance [?], abstinence with [?], zeal without harshness,
gentleness with justice, trust without neglect, fear without despair, poverty without pride, confession without excuses,
teaching with practice, climbing without falling, lowly towards the lofty, smooth towards the rough, work without grumbling, simplicity with prudence,
humility without favouritism [?], Christianity without hypocrisy [?]. All these are contained in renunciation.
A person is pure when they are full of charity: they go about with charity, they reject every evil, they love every good.
Such a person is honoured on earth and glorified in heaven. Love God, and everyone will love you. Fear God, and everyone will fear you.
This, then, is the rule of clerical life, and this is the measured devotion according to God.
Whoever submits to it [?] and fulfils it [?] will strike down [?] the hundred devils of the earth and will have the kingdom of heaven.
Everyone should beseech and pray to the Lord of heaven and earth that fear and love of him be nurtured in their heart,
for it is through the nurturing [?] of a person that the fear of God would enter their heart.
As long as fear is weak, repentance will be weak. As long as repentance is weak, Christianity will be weak.
For whoever has no fear of God will have no love of him; whoever has no love of him
will not keep his commandments; whoever does not keep his commandments will not have life in heaven.
For fear brings love, love brings pure deeds, and pure deeds bring eternal life in heaven.
The love of God washes the soul, satisfies the mind, increases the reward, drives out vices, and despises [?] the earth: it washes, it binds [?], it [?].
What does the love of God do for a person? It kills their desires, cleanses their heart, and keeps them holy [?],
drives out [?] their vices, earns rewards, [?] life, and washes the soul.
There are four remedies for the soul: fear and repentance, love and hope. Two of them hold firm [?] on earth; the other two raise one up to heaven.
Fear guards against the sins that lie ahead; repentance washes away the sins that have gone before.
Love of the Creator and hope of his kingdom are what raise one up to heaven.
So whoever fears God and loves him and fulfils his will and his commandments
will be honoured before people in this world and will be blessed with God in the next.
What is good for a person? That is: steadfastness in renunciation, restraint [?] of speech, gentle brotherliness,
giving with readiness [?], keeping the rule without transgression, rising at the first [?] call, and a step of obedience for God,
forgiveness of [?], tending [?] the sick, diligence in prayer, fasting with [?] (one's fellows?), [?] (sharing?) with one's neighbour,
humbling of pride, sincerity from the heart, breaking of one's will, subduing of one's nature, patience in tribulations.
What does that do for you? Not hard to say. A summons to the elders, a seat of [?],
wealth from someone whom one does not [?], honour without striving, a hundredfold in many things, [?] (their friendship?) with the brethren, eternal life in heaven.
What should a religious person avoid? Not hard to say.
Frequent anger, pride without skill and without substance, rashness towards the superior, slowness at the bell,
conversation with [?] (unseemly people?), being flighty, mocking words, impure words, harshness of reply,
lingering with the prior [?], making peace with reproach [?], [?] (sharing an inheritance?) with monks, frequent complaining.
What does that do for you? Not hard to say. Separation from the elders, work without [?] (profit?), [?],
hostility from people, fasting without reward, rising in the dark [without benefit?], the blackening of one's patron saint [?], hell instead of heaven.
It is right for us that the vices should not deceive us in place of the virtues, for they could be chosen [instead]:
laxity in place of mercy, [?] (sullen concealment?) in place of truth, [?] (disobedience?) in place of uprightness, fear of [?] (others' displeasure?) without defending the truth,
without [open] proclamation [of it]; iniquity in place of humility, stinginess and [?] in place of [?] (generosity?), pride in place of chastity,
boasting in place of abstinence, wastefulness and squandering in place of generosity, unmeasured anger in place of spiritual zeal,
excessive fear and [?] in place of quiet humility, hardness and cunning in place of steadfastness, [?] and flightiness in place of [?] (fasting?),
great [?] (transgression?) and restlessness in place of [?], laziness and idleness in place of freedom [?], excessive [?] (praise?) in place of counsel.
Whoever is in the unity of the Catholic Church, and in hope of the heavenly expectation, and fulfils the commandments as they were taught,
will have the hundredfold on earth and will have eternal life in heaven.
If there is anyone who desires the truth, it is right for him to have knowledge of its proper ways: what hides it and what reveals it.
Truth is hidden from everyone who [?] (opposes it?); it is revealed to everyone who fulfils the truth.
Four things cover up the truth, namely love and fear, [?] and [?] (need?).
As long as a person is unrighteous, he cannot proclaim the truth properly.
Three things lie in wait for them: vanity, pride and anger.
If anyone gives way before him, it rouses vanity in him; if he is opposed, it rouses anger and pride in him,
for there are many who are zealous about the truth, but they [?] (are angry?) with it [?].
There are two things to beware of in zeal for righteousness: anger and [?] (altes),
for whichever of them comes upon it is a stain on righteousness. For zeal for righteousness is fitting if its proper rules are kept:
zeal without anger; humility without neglect of righteousness, however it is proclaimed; along with humility without contentiousness,
for the humble person does not contend against unrighteousness [?] (cammaif).
A person is not righteous unless he is truly humble; he is not truly wise unless he is righteous.
For true wisdom finds no place alongside a person's unrighteousness, for the veil between them is thick,
for it is nearer to meet with the wisdom of righteousness than with the righteousness of wisdom.
For a person is truly wise when he is righteous, so that he speaks the truth without bitterness and without contention, with patience and with gentleness.
Wealth and wisdom and true piety reach a person together. When do they reach a person?
When his righteousness is perfect [?] (n-dílacht). When is his righteousness perfect [?]?
When his heart is in its proper state, then that is righteousness, as if [?] (amail ní roichned ó duini).
The fifteen strengths of the soul: the strength of faith, the strength of gentleness, the strength of humility,
the strength of patience, the strength of mortification, the strength of obedience, the strength of love, the strength of righteousness, the strength of mercy,
the strength of generosity, the strength of restraint [?] (fúarrigi), the strength of [?] (comalti), the strength of wealth, the strength of piety, the strength of almsgiving.
The person who practises these strengths [?] (di sunt lelaill) will escape [?] his testing in fire, and will gain [?] a patron [?] in heaven.
When is a person able to be a witness [?] over the souls of others? When he has first been a witness over his own soul.
When is he able to correct another? When he has first corrected himself.

A person who turns his own soul to life, however many souls he may turn [?], all the people of the world, provided they were teachable, he would turn them to life so that they would be in the kingdom of heaven.
The one who does not correct himself [?], his evil and his [?] (vallbe) drive him away from the kingdom of God. The body protects the soul,
the soul protects the mind, the mind protects the heart, the heart protects faith, faith protects God, God protects the person.
As a lamp sends up its light in a dark house, so righteousness rises up in the midst of faith in a person's heart.
Four darknesses drive it out from where it rises:
the darkness of paganism, the darkness of ignorance, the darkness of unbelief, and the darkness of sin, so that it finds no place there.
Three come to piety. One is in it, another is near it, another is far from it.
They are not equal, however. It is better for the one who is in it than for the one who is near it.
It is better for the one who is near it than for the one who is far from it.
The one who is in it is the one who [?] every day the three things by which the life of his soul is obtained, namely:
whatever good he has heard and whatever good he has seen, he has loved, believed and fulfilled.
The one who is near it is the one who renounces the world with his lips but holds on to it in his heart.
He resists it with fasting and prayer, but he has not [?] cast off greed and [?]; one hand toward [?heaven], the other toward the earth.
The one who is far from it is the one who [?] and does not practise its ways according to the goodness of his life [?].
For him it would be easier to do anything [?] else.
Three enemies of the soul: the world, the devil, and an impure teacher.
Three things that restrain a wandering spirit and make a steady mind:
vigil, prayer and labour. Four comforts of piety: patience against every desire,
coolness against every unkindness, [?forbearance] toward every wrong, forgiveness of every [?provocation].
Four sayings that would [?save] us if we fulfilled them: zeal toward God,
kindness toward people, goodwill toward every single person, preparation for death every single day.
Four things that do not happen to anyone who loves God: he is not [?mocked], he is not [?],
he does not revile, he is not suspected by anyone. He is good in everyone's eyes, and everyone is good in his.
Four safeguards of the children of life: mortification of their desires, fear of the torments, love of tribulations, belief in the rewards.
If they did not mortify their desires, they would not give them up; if they did not fear the torments, they would not beware of them;
if they did not love tribulations, they would not endure them; if they did not believe in the rewards, they would not attain them.
Four locks of the sinners: the closing of their eyes to the world, the closing of the earth over their bodies,
the closing of the kingdom of heaven against their souls, the closing of hell upon them.
Four wedges of the sinners: a wedge for them so that they do not abandon their desires, a wedge so that they do not go into the torments [?],
a wedge without repentance after [?], a wedge without their dwelling in the kingdom.
Four things that bring [?outlawry / the life of a fían] upon a person: it [?diminishes] territories, increases enmities, cuts life short, and brings on torments [?].
Four things by which the kingdom of God is gained: stability and freedom from the world, zeal and perseverance.
Four blessings of a person in this present world: youth and prosperity, health and many friends.
A person has four hells in this world: sickness and old age, poverty and wretchedness.
There are three things through which the devil can be seen in a person: through the face, through the gait, through the speech. And through these three, God is understood through a person.
The three waves that go over a person at baptism, through the renunciation he makes in them, namely:
he renounces the world with its desires, he renounces the devil with his snares, he renounces the desires of the flesh.
This is what brings it about that a person who was a son of death becomes a son of life, and one who was a son of darkness becomes a son of light.
Alas for anyone who breaks these three renunciations made in the three waves that went over him!
Unless he comes through a flood again, he will not go into the kingdom of God, namely a flood of tears of repentance, a flood of blood squeezed out in penance, a flood of sweat in [?].
What is best for piety? Simplicity and sincerity.
Idle piety, practised with great toil [?]: its testing in fire will be great, its reward in heaven will be small.
Active piety, practised for great consolation [?]: its testing in fire will be small, its reward in heaven will be great.
What is best for the mind? Breadth and humility, for every good thing takes hold in a broad, humble mind.
What is worst for the mind? Narrowness, hardness and constriction, for no good thing fits in a narrow, hard, constricted mind.
Will [?] and youth, death and old age: it is best to be far from them while awaiting them [?]. He does not ask [?], he does not refuse, [?] from his wealth [?].
He consents and does not proclaim; he commands and does not forbid [?]; he conceals, he listens in silence, he reflects, he [?].
If anyone desires the commandments, let him take the road on which they all go, namely:
let him take charity, humility and patience into his heart, for in that way he will not break [?] the commandments, but all of them will be complete in him.
Whom should we consider prudent [?]? The one who obtains before death what he will need after death.
Gentle correction, not harsh rebuke: rebuke stirs up the mind [?], for the mind is humble toward correction.
Wisdom without learning is better than learning without wisdom.
Who is nearest to God? The one who is humble. Whom does Christ help? The one who does good.
In whom does the Holy Spirit dwell? In the one who is pure, without sin.
A person becomes a vessel of the Holy Spirit when the virtues have come in place of the vices.
The will of God grows in a person when he loves [?perhaps 'forsakes'] worldly desire. It is better for us to prepare for the five meetings we shall come to, namely:
the meeting with sickness [?], the meeting with death, the meeting with the household of God, the meeting with demons, the meeting with the resurrection on the Day of Judgement.
The End. Amen.
